text:
Kira: We hit a weird one in the staging multi-region run: active/active allowed reads from local region but writes fell back and violated a tenant residency constraint.
Sam: can you summarize what the sequence was?
Kira: brief: tenant T-842 was pinned to ap-southeast. ap-southeast started returning intermittent 500s from the model-serving pool. Our proxy fallback sent writes to us-east which accepted them. Control plane metadata still said ap-southeast-only.
Omar: did the control plane ever revoke the residency?
Kira: no, allocation remained ap-southeast. The proxy fallback path doesn't consult the control plane allocation on failover, only on initial routing.
Tess: so gap between allocation assertion and fallback behavior. That's dangerous. We need a stronger, machine-verifiable assertion.
Sam: proposal: control plane issues a signed short-lived residency token when it allocates a tenant placement. Example header: 

X-Tenant-Residency: tenant=T-842;region=ap-southeast;exp=1700000000;sig=v1:abcd1234

Proxy must validate signature and expiry before accepting writes in a different region. If validation fails, return 451 or queue writes for manual approval.
Omar: signed token is good but increases crypto ops on the data path. Could we instead make the proxy query a tiny placement cache service (local LRU) that stores allocation assertions with TTL? That keeps signatures off the hot path.
Tess: both can work: cache for fast-path, signed token as fallback or for cross-cluster validation. Also need to instrument metrics: cross-region-write-attempts, rejected-fallbacks, manual-override-count.
Kira: operator flow suggestion: when proxy rejects a fallback due to residency mismatch, automatically create a tenant quarantine incident and surface an "expedite override" button that requires two approvers and logs who clicked it. The button issues a one-shot override token valid for 10 minutes.
Sam: agree on guardrails. Also add a safety check in the sweep service: detect recent cross-region writes and trigger data reconcile if any stray writes occurred.
Omar: we should add tests: a fault-injection harness that simulates partition and asserts no writes land outside allowed region, unless override path used and audited. Add to chaos tests.
Tess: long-term refactor: introduce a Residency API (GET /v1/residency/{tenant}) returning a small canonical struct. Expose client libs for proxy and operator tools. That helps avoid duplicated logic.
Kira: timeline: spike the placement-cache + metrics this sprint. Sam could you own the canary for token validation?
Sam: yep, will spin up a canary proxy with placement-cache enabled and synthetic tenants. infra-bot: canary deployment scheduled: placement-cache-canary -> staging at 2026-03-23T09:40Z 🚀
Omar: also need to update runbooks with clear rollback and data-recovery steps. I'll draft suggested wording.
Tess: don't forget kv-cache priming: when we change placement we need to invalidate or prime caches across regions to avoid stale acceptance. Add a placement-change webhook for proxies.
Kira: good point. Add action items: 1) design placement cache + token hybrid (Sam/Omar) 2) residency API RFC (Tess) 3) runbook updates & override flow (Omar) 4) chaos test for cross-region writes (Kira) 5) metrics/dashboard (Sam). Target: roll canary + runbook edits by 2026-03-29.
Sam: I'll open PRs by EOD and tag reviewers.
Omar: will write runbook draft and incident template.
Tess: will start residency API RFC doc.
Kira: thanks all. Let's avoid a production surprise like this.
infra-bot: monitoring alert rule created: cross_region_write_attempts > 0 -> notify #incidents + create incident draft.
